title: Cross (vector) product
examples: How do I find the area of a parallelogram using vectors?
What is the normal vector to a plane defined by two vectors?
Can I use the cross product to find the area of a triangle?

explain.say: Today we learn about the cross product of vectors. It gives us useful geometric information. One key use is finding the area of a parallelogram.
If you have two vectors, say a and b, forming two sides. The magnitude of their cross product gives the area. Think of the vectors starting from the same point.

items: Vectors a and b form sides

explain.say: For example, if a is three i plus two j, and b is one i plus four j. You calculate the cross product a cross b. The magnitude of that result is your area.
Another important use is finding a normal vector. This vector sticks straight out, perpendicular to the plane formed by a and b. You calculate a cross b, and that result is the normal vector.

items: Perpendicular to plane of a and b

explain.say: Consider vectors a and b again. The vector a cross b points normal to the plane. This vector is perpendicular to both a and b simultaneously. This is a key property to remember.

draw.text: Perpendicular to both a and b

faq.q: How do I find the area of a triangle using the cross product?
faq.a: The area of a triangle formed by two vectors a and b is half the magnitude of their cross product. You calculate |a cross b| and then divide the result by two.
asks: What is the area of a triangle with vectors?
How do I use cross product for triangle area?

faq.q: What does the cross product tell me about the orientation?
faq.a: The direction of the resulting vector follows the right-hand rule. If you curl your fingers from the first vector to the second, your thumb points in the direction of the cross product.
asks: Does the order matter for the cross product?
How do I know which way the normal vector points?

faq.a: No, the cross product is not commutative. This means that a cross b is not equal to b cross a. In fact, b cross a is the negative of a cross b.
asks: Is a x b the same as b x a?
What is the relationship between a x b and b x a?

faq.q: When should I use the cross product instead of dot product?
faq.a: Use the cross product when you need a vector perpendicular to two other vectors. Use the dot product when you need the angle or projection between them.
asks: When is cross product better than dot product?
What is the difference between cross and dot product?

faq.q: Does the magnitude of the cross product depend on the angle?
faq.a: Yes, the magnitude is largest when the vectors are perpendicular, giving the maximum area. It is zero when the vectors are parallel or anti-parallel.
asks: What happens to |a x b| if a and b are parallel?
How does the angle affect the cross product magnitude?

facts: The magnitude of the cross product of two vectors a and b is given by |a| |b| sin(theta).
The resulting vector a cross b is perpendicular (normal) to the plane containing a and b.
The cross product is anti-commutative, meaning a cross b = - (b cross a).
The cross product of any vector with itself is the zero vector, so a cross a = 0.

quiz.say: If vector a is (2, 0, 0) and vector b is (0, 3, 0), what is the magnitude of a cross b?
quiz.why: The vectors lie on the x and y axes, forming a right angle. The magnitude is simply the product of the lengths, 2 times 3, which is 6.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the vectors are perpendicular, not parallel.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you are adding the components, not finding the area.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the magnitude is a scalar value, not a vector component.

quiz.say: If a cross b results in a vector pointing straight up the z-axis, what is the relationship between a and b?
quiz.show: a and b are perpendicular to z-axis

options.show: a and b are in the xy-plane
options.say: a and b are in the xy-plane

quiz.why: A vector pointing along the z-axis is normal to the xy-plane. Therefore, the two original vectors must also lie within that plane.

wrong.1: If they were parallel, the cross product would be zero, not pointing up.
wrong.2: Collinear means they are on the same line, resulting in a zero cross product.
wrong.3: Anti-parallel means they point opposite ways, which also results in a zero cross product.

quiz.say: To find the normal vector to the plane defined by vectors a and b, what operation must you perform?
quiz.why: The cross product of two non-parallel vectors always yields a resultant vector perpendicular to the plane they define.

wrong.0: The dot product gives a scalar value related to the angle, not a perpendicular vector.
wrong.1: Adding vectors results in a vector that lies in the same plane as a and b.
wrong.2: This operation is not defined for finding a normal vector in this context.
